title: How to build a recruiter-friendly resume with AI
excerpt: A practical guide to writing clearer sections, stronger bullets, and cleaner exports before your next application.
author: CareerBOT Team
body: Recruiters spend seconds, not minutes, scanning a resume before deciding whether to read further. That means structure and clarity matter as much as the work you've actually done.

Start with a clean section order: contact details, a short professional summary, experience, skills, and education. Avoid tables, columns, or graphics that can break when a resume is parsed by an applicant tracking system.

Every bullet under your experience should follow a simple pattern: what you did, how you did it, and the measurable result. "Improved onboarding flow" says little. "Redesigned onboarding flow, cutting new-hire setup time from 45 to 12 minutes" gives a recruiter something concrete to remember.

Once the structure is solid, use AI suggestions to tighten language rather than invent achievements. The best use of AI here is editing — turning a vague draft into a sharper, metric-backed version of something you actually did.
Before you export, check that your formatting survives a plain-text copy-paste. If your bullets, headers, and dates still read cleanly with no styling, an ATS will parse them correctly too.
